rationale:
Both replace the character-scanning state machine with a clear line-based parser and helper functions. B's structure is cleaner. Each list item is emitted as a complete
  • ...
    • , rather than A's approach of leaving the open and closing it on the next item or on list close. B uses local closures over a paragraph buffer, while A passes a *strings.Builder and a *bool to free helper functions, which is clunkier. B's switch gives each construct exactly one case, and its doc comment documents the grammar well. A's per-line emphasis is arguably more sensible than B's whole-document pre-pass. However, A's comment claims it matches the original behavior when it actually differs, whereas B states its choice honestly. Overall B is more readable and maintainable.
